question: How do I log in to QMS RISE?
answer: Open the QMS RISE website. On the splash screen click "Skip Intro" or wait for it to finish, then click "Use email & password instead" if the face login does not appear. Enter your UNIMY email and password and click Login.

question: Can I log in with my face?
answer: Yes. On the login screen, click "Use Face Login instead" and allow camera access. Position your face inside the circle and hold still. If it fails, click "Try Again" or fall back to email and password.

question: I forgot my password. What do I do?
answer: Click "Forgot password?" on the login screen. Enter your registered email and follow the reset link sent to your inbox. If you do not receive it, contact your lecturer or the QMS admin.

question: Why can't I log in?
answer: Check that you are using your UNIMY email (not a personal one), your password is correct (case-sensitive), and your account is active. If you still cannot log in, contact your lecturer or the So-CSI admin office.

question: How do I log out safely?
answer: Click your name or profile icon in the top-right corner, then click Logout. Always log out on shared devices. A logout video may play automatically.

question: What is on my student dashboard?
answer: The dashboard shows your RISE Score, RISE Categories grid, Quick Actions tiles, recent activity, notifications, and shortcuts to attendance, quizzes, evaluations, timetable, and support tools.

question: How do I customise my dashboard?
answer: Drag any RISE Category card to reorder it. Drag a card onto the Quick Actions grid to pin it as a shortcut. Your order is saved automatically and follows you across devices.

question: What are Quick Actions?
answer: Quick Actions are shortcut tiles at the bottom of your dashboard. You can pin up to 6 by dragging a RISE Category card onto the grid. Click the Edit button in the header to remove a pinned tile.

question: How do I reset my dashboard layout?
answer: Open the browser console and type resetDashboardOrder() and press Enter. The dashboard will reload with the default order.

question: What are RISE Points?
answer: RISE Points are points you earn for engagement: attendance, evaluations, quizzes, events, workshops, certifications, competitions, clubs, streak activity, community service, and research. They build your tier and unlock badges.

question: How do I earn RISE Points?
answer: You earn points by scanning QR attendance, submitting evaluations, playing Quiz Battle, joining events and workshops, uploading Coursera certificates, participating in clubs, maintaining a streak, competing in competitions, doing community service, and contributing to research.

question: What are RISE Tiers?
answer: Tiers are levels based on your total RISE Points. Higher tiers unlock badges and recognition. Check your tier on the dashboard card labelled RISE Score.

question: Where can I see my RISE Points history?
answer: Open My Progress or your Profile page. You will see a breakdown of every point-earning activity with the date, category, and points awarded.

question: What is a Streak?
answer: A streak tracks consecutive days or weeks of engagement. Keep using QMS every day to build and maintain your streak for bonus points.

question: Do points expire?
answer: Points do not expire within an active academic year. They are tied to your student account and carry forward with your programme.

question: What are RISE Categories?
answer: RISE Categories are the 12 areas of engagement the QMS tracks: Attendance, Evaluation, Quiz Battle, Bonus, Clubs & Roles, Streak, Workshops & Talks, Competitions, Coursera, Award & Recognition, Community Service, and Research & Publications.

question: How do I see my progress in a category?
answer: Click on a RISE Category card to open its detail page. It shows your current points, max cap, and recent activity.

question: What are category caps?
answer: Each category has a maximum point cap per semester. Once you hit the cap, extra activity still counts for your record but does not add points.

question: What are badges?
answer: Badges are digital awards you unlock by hitting milestones: attendance streaks, high quiz scores, tier upgrades, club roles, event participation, and more.

question: Where can I see my badges?
answer: Open Awards & Recognition from the dashboard or navigate to your Profile. All earned badges appear with the date they were unlocked.

question: How do I earn a new badge?
answer: Keep engaging: attend classes, play quizzes, submit evaluations, join events, earn certificates. Progress toward the next badge is shown on your Awards page.

question: How do I check in to attendance using QR?
answer: Go to QR Scanner from Quick Actions or the sidebar. Point your camera at the QR code shown by your lecturer and hold steady. The system detects the code, marks your attendance, and credits RISE Points.

question: What if the QR camera does not work?
answer: Click Start Camera again and allow camera access when prompted. If it still fails, type the session code manually in the input box and press "Mark Attendance".

question: How fast do I need to scan the QR?
answer: The QR regenerates every 15 seconds, so scan quickly. If you miss the window, wait for the next code to appear and scan again.

question: Why does it say "Invalid or expired code"?
answer: The code expired before you submitted, or you typed it wrong. Wait for the lecturer to display a new QR, then scan or type the new code immediately.

question: Why does it say "Already checked in"?
answer: You cannot check in twice for the same session. If you think this is a mistake, contact your lecturer so they can review the session log.

question: Where do I see my attendance record?
answer: Open Attendance from the sidebar. You will see every session you attended with subject, type, location, date, and points earned.

question: What is attendance bonus?
answer: Attendance bonus is extra RISE Points awarded for consistent attendance or hitting attendance milestones.

question: Does attendance affect my grade?
answer: Attendance contributes to your RISE Score and engagement profile. It does not directly change a course grade but is visible to staff and factored into engagement reports.

question: What types of attendance sessions exist?
answer: Session types include class, lab, workshop, event, and bonus. Each type carries a different point value.

question: What is Quiz Battle Arena?
answer: Quiz Battle Arena is a live 1-on-1 quiz feature. You choose 5, 10, or 20 questions, the system matches you with another student from your programme, a 3-second countdown starts, and you both answer to score highest.

question: How do I start a quiz?
answer: Go to Quiz Battle Arena from the sidebar or dashboard. Choose your topic, choose 5/10/20 questions, click Find Opponent, and wait for the countdown.

question: How are quiz points calculated?
answer: You earn RISE Points for correct answers and a bonus for winning the battle. Faster correct answers may earn extra points.

question: Can I see past quiz results?
answer: Yes. Open Quiz Battle Arena and click History or Results. You will see every match, opponent, score, and points earned.

question: What topics are in the quiz?
answer: Quiz topics follow your enrolled courses. Each course may have its own question set managed by your lecturer.

question: What if I disconnect during a quiz?
answer: If you lose connection mid-quiz you may forfeit the match. Reconnect quickly and re-enter the arena. Forfeited matches do not count toward your score.

question: How do I submit an evaluation?
answer: Open Evaluation from the sidebar. Select a lecturer, choose the week, rate each criterion from 1 to 10 using the sliders, then click Submit.

question: How often can I submit evaluations?
answer: You submit one evaluation per lecturer per week. Repeated submissions in the same week are blocked.

question: Is my evaluation anonymous?
answer: Your submission is stored but shown to staff in aggregated form. Staff cannot see your identity in individual responses.

question: What is the evaluation score based on?
answer: You rate teaching quality, clarity, engagement, pacing, materials, and support on a 1-10 scale. The average appears in staff evaluation reports.

question: Can I change my evaluation after submitting?
answer: No. Once submitted, evaluations are locked. If you submitted by mistake, contact your lecturer.

question: What is Study Plan?
answer: Study Plan shows your planned courses across semesters. It helps you see prerequisites, track progression, and plan your pathway.

question: How do I build a study plan?
answer: Open Study Plan from the sidebar. Drag courses from the available list into the semester buckets. The system checks prerequisites and credit-hour rules automatically.

question: What are prerequisites?
answer: Prerequisites are courses you must pass before you can take a higher course. The Study Plan flags any course whose prerequisites are not met.

question: Can I move a course to a different semester?
answer: Yes. Drag the course card to another semester bucket. The plan saves automatically.

question: Where do I see my timetable?
answer: Open Timetable from the sidebar. It shows your weekly class schedule with subject, time, location, and lecturer.

question: Can I export my timetable?
answer: Use your browser's print option (Ctrl+P) to save the timetable as PDF. Spreadsheet export is available if enabled by your school.

question: What is Enrolment Request?
answer: Enrolment Request lets you formally request to register for a subject. It replaces informal email requests and tracks the approval workflow.

question: How do I submit an enrolment request?
answer: Open Enrolment Requests, click New Request, choose the subject and semester, add a reason if required, and submit. You will see the status change as it moves through approval.

question: What does an exception request mean?
answer: If you do not meet prerequisites, you can request an exception with a written reason. Your HOP will review it.

question: What is Credit Transfer?
answer: Credit Transfer lets you apply to have courses from another institution counted toward your UNIMY programme.

question: How do I apply for Credit Transfer?
answer: Open Credit Transfers, click New Application, upload your transcript and course syllabus, list the courses you want transferred, and submit.

question: How long does review take?
answer: Review is handled by your HOP and Dean. You can track the status in the Credit Transfer page. Most decisions are returned within two weeks.

question: Who decides my credit transfer?
answer: Your HOP reviews the course matching, and the Dean approves the final decision. You will see comments in the Credit Transfer page.

question: How do I see events?
answer: Open Events from the sidebar. Upcoming events are listed with date, time, venue, points offered, and seats remaining.

question: How do I book an event?
answer: Click Book on the event card. Your booking is confirmed instantly if seats are available. You will receive a confirmation and any points after attendance is marked.

question: Can I cancel an event booking?
answer: Yes. Open Events, find the booked event, and click Cancel. Cancellations after the deadline may affect points.

question: Do events give RISE Points?
answer: Most events, workshops, talks, and competitions carry RISE Points. The exact amount is shown on the event card.

question: What are Clubs & Roles?
answer: Clubs are student organisations. Roles are positions inside a club (President, Secretary, etc.) that carry additional points and recognition.

question: How do I join a club?
answer: Open Clubs & Roles, browse active clubs, click Join, and wait for approval from the club leader or Dean.

question: Do clubs have their own events?
answer: Yes. Many clubs run events, competitions, and workshops. Club event attendance also counts toward your RISE Points.

question: What is Award & Recognition?
answer: Awards and Recognition highlight outstanding student achievement across academics, engagement, and service. Your dashboard shows any awards you have received.

question: How do I get nominated for an award?
answer: Nominations come from staff based on engagement, RISE Points, and academic record. There is no self-nomination.

question: What is a Certificate in QMS?
answer: Certificates are formal records you can submit as evidence of external learning (Coursera, edX, professional bodies). Once approved, they appear on your profile.

question: How do I submit a Coursera certificate?
answer: Open Coursera from the sidebar, upload a PDF or image of your certificate, select the linked course, and submit. Reviewers approve it and points are credited.

question: How many Coursera points can I earn?
answer: The Coursera category has a semester cap. Each approved certificate adds a fixed amount until you reach the cap.

question: How do I send a message?
answer: Open Messages from the sidebar, choose a recipient from your contacts, type your message, and press Send. Messages are stored in your conversation history.

question: Who can I message?
answer: You can message your lecturers, HOP, and other students who have accepted your chat request. You cannot message users who have blocked you.

question: Do I get notifications for new messages?
answer: Yes. A badge shows unread messages in the sidebar. You can manage notification preferences in your Profile page.

question: What is Peer Chat?
answer: Peer Chat lets you connect with other students. You send a request, they accept, and then you can chat freely. You can block anyone at any time.

question: How do I send a peer chat request?
answer: Open Peer Chat, search for a student by name or ID, click Send Request. They will receive a notification and can accept or reject.

question: How do I block someone?
answer: Open the conversation, click the menu (three dots), and select Block. Blocked users cannot message you or send new requests.

question: What does the online dot mean?
answer: The green dot next to a name means the student is currently online in QMS. Grey means offline.

question: How do I file a complaint?
answer: Open Complaints from the sidebar, click New Complaint, choose a category, describe the issue, and submit. You can choose to file anonymously.

question: Who sees my complaint?
answer: Only authorised staff (Dean, HOP, and assigned reviewers) see complaints. Other students never see your complaint.

question: Can I file anonymously?
answer: Yes. Toggle the Anonymous option when submitting. Your identity is hidden from reviewers but recorded for audit purposes only.

question: What is Academic Support?
answer: Academic Support is where you request help with studies, ask for tutoring, flag difficulty in a subject, or ask for a meeting with a lecturer.

question: How do I request academic support?
answer: Open Academic Support, describe your issue, choose the subject, and submit. Your lecturer or HOP will respond.

question: How do I upload a document?
answer: Open Documents from the sidebar, click Upload, choose your file (PDF, image, or Office document), and attach it to the correct folder.

question: What file types are allowed?
answer: PDF, PNG, JPG, DOCX, and DOC are supported. Maximum size is typically 10 MB per file. Ask your lecturer if a different format is required.

question: Who can see my uploads?
answer: Only you and the staff you share them with. Documents are protected by role-based access.

question: What is the AI Assistant?
answer: The AI Assistant is the floating chat button at the bottom-right of the screen. It answers questions about QMS using the QMS knowledge base and can help with common tasks.

question: How do I open the AI Assistant?
answer: Click the round robot button at the bottom-right, or press Ctrl+K on desktop. The chat panel opens with suggested questions.

question: Does the AI Assistant know everything?
answer: It answers from the QMS FAQ knowledge base and can supplement with general AI. For academic decisions always confirm with your lecturer or HOP.

question: How do I edit my profile?
answer: Click your avatar in the top-right, choose Profile, and update your photo, contact details, and preferences. Some fields (name, student ID) cannot be changed.

question: How do I change my avatar?
answer: Open Profile, click the avatar image, choose from the avatar catalog, and save. You can also upload your own photo.

question: How do I change my password?
answer: Open Profile, scroll to Security, click Change Password, enter your current password and the new one twice.

question: How do I manage notification preferences?
answer: Open Profile, scroll to Notifications, and toggle which alerts you want by email, in-app, or both.

question: Does QMS work on my phone?
answer: Yes. QMS is fully responsive. The dashboard, attendance, quizzes, and chat all work on mobile browsers. Some features like QR scanning require camera permission.

question: Why is the layout broken on my phone?
answer: Try rotating your device, or clear the browser cache and reload. If a specific page is broken, report it with a screenshot.

question: Do I need to install an app?
answer: No. QMS RISE runs entirely in the browser. Just bookmark it on your home screen for one-tap access.

question: How is my data protected?
answer: QMS uses role-based access and Row Level Security at the database level. Only you and authorised staff can see your records. All traffic uses HTTPS.

question: Can staff see my face login data?
answer: Face credentials are stored separately and only used to verify your identity. Staff cannot view your face data.

question: What should I do if I suspect unauthorised access?
answer: Change your password immediately, then contact your lecturer or the So-CSI admin. You can also check active sessions in Profile → Security.

question: What is CLO Attainment?
answer: Course Learning Outcome (CLO) Attainment measures how well students achieve the intended learning outcomes of a course. It is a staff-reviewed record and not shown to students on their dashboard.

question: What is CQI?
answer: Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) is how staff record and act on quality issues. Students benefit indirectly by improvements to courses and teaching. Students do not see CQI records.

question: What is the QS1 paper?
answer: QS1 papers are quality-system assessment records used by staff for review and accreditation. They are not visible to students.

question: How do I find something quickly?
answer: Use the AI Assistant (Ctrl+K) or the FAQ search. You can type any keyword — attendance, quiz, points, evaluation, certificate — and it will find matching help.

question: Who do I contact for QMS issues?
answer: Contact your lecturer first. If it is a system problem, contact the So-CSI admin office or Dean's office. For urgent issues, use the Complaints page.
